title: TMC's Abhishek Banerjee Was Attacked With Bricks and Stones in Sonarpur. Five People Have Been Arrested.
excerpt: The assault on Mamata Banerjee's nephew — who was visiting families affected by post-poll violence in West Bengal — has become a flashpoint in the state's bitter political transition.
body:
Trinamool Congress MP Abhishek Banerjee was attacked by a mob on Saturday during a visit to Sonarpur in South 24 Parganas district, in one of the most violent incidents since the BJP's victory in West Bengal's 2026 assembly elections. Five people have since been arrested, and the incident has opened a new front in the state's increasingly bitter political transition.

Banerjee, who is also the nephew of former Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee, had gone to South Sonarpur to meet families of TMC workers who said they had been targeted in post-poll violence. According to party leaders, a group of protesters — reportedly BJP supporters — surrounded his vehicle, raised slogans, and pelted him with bricks, stones, eggs, and shoes. His shirt was torn in the scuffle, and he sustained an injury near his eye from a brick.

"They hit my eye with a brick, and I can't open my eye," Banerjee said afterward, visibly shaken. "I was wearing a helmet, otherwise my head would have been split in two."

## The Arrests

West Bengal Police arrested five people in connection with the attack following overnight raids on Sunday. The accused — Akash Gayen, Kajal Das, Debashish Dutta, Nirmalya Sengupta, and Tapan Maiti — were identified through video footage from the scene and produced before the Baruipur court on Sunday. A case has been registered at Sonarpur Police Station.

Banerjee blamed the BJP for orchestrating the attack, calling it "all BJP-sponsored" and pointing to the absence of police during the assault. "It hasn't even been a month, and the police are nowhere to be seen," he told ANI.

## Mamata Banerjee's Response

Former Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee visited her nephew at a Kolkata hospital and described the attack as a "pre-planned conspiracy." She said blood clots had formed following the assault and questioned why hospital authorities had initially admitted him to the Intensive Therapy Unit before shifting him — alleging that BJP leaders and a senior police officer pressured the hospital to discharge him early.

"If he had not been wearing a helmet, he could have died on the spot," she told reporters.

## The BJP's Counter

The BJP has pushed back against TMC's characterisation of the incident. State BJP president Samik Bhattacharya condemned the violence but said it reflected public anger against the former ruling party, not a state-sponsored operation. He issued an appeal for restraint while pointedly reminding reporters of Abhishek Banerjee's "provocative" campaign speeches before the elections — speeches for which an FIR has already been registered.

The CPI(M), West Bengal's other major opposition party, struck a similar tone: condemning the violence while noting that the TMC's own record on political violence during its years in power had set the template now being used against it.

## The Bigger Picture

The attack on Abhishek Banerjee is not an isolated incident. Since the BJP's victory in the West Bengal assembly elections, reports of post-poll violence have emerged from multiple districts. Both the TMC and the BJP have accused each other of targeting the other side's workers and supporters.

For the Indian diaspora watching West Bengal's political transition from abroad, the Sonarpur incident is a reminder that the state's elections are rarely decided at the ballot box alone. The violence that follows is often as consequential — and as defining — as the vote itself.

Banerjee, despite his injuries, has signalled he will not be deterred. "You can make my body fall," he said from the hospital, "but my resolve is strong, and this head won't bow down."
